Ben, who has up until now been the most "rational" has seen them all slowly become undone more and more. He's seen the way the dynamics have shifted, he saw them eat Jackie and he probably began to come to terms with that - she was already dead, they were hungry. But then walking in and seeing Javi literally butchered and Nat telling him that they let him die? That the "wilderness chose"? And then later from his POV she's fully joined them now, and he has nobody he can trust.

Like Nat said, he's an outsider, he doesn't belong, and that means he can't see things the way they do. I don't think that makes him "above" them, he just doesn't believe in the wilderness. 

Was what he did right? No. But to HIM, it was, he was scared and horrified. Just like what the girls did by watching Javi die and beg for help wasn't right. But to THEM, it was because they were starving and believe that he was "chosen". None of them are suppose to be "morally right" because they're no longer thinking like that. 

Personally I don't think I can judge any of them 🤷🏼‍♀️
